summary: Introductory partner-fit call between Redwood (AE+SE+CSM) and PolarisIQ platform + infra leads. Main goals: assess channel/reseller alignment, identify integration friction (VPC/private deployments, KV cache routing, billing/commissions), and scope a short pilot for performance benchmarking. Action items captured and next steps planned for security docs and benchmark run.
transcript:
Meeting header: 2027-03-04 16:00 PT | Duration 46m | Attendees: Maya, Jonah, Luca (Redwood) -- Priya, Raj, Alex (PolarisIQ)

00:00 Maya: hey everyone thanks for joining, can you hear me ok?
00:05 Priya: yes loud and clear, thanks Maya, excited to learn about how Redwood might fit in our channel/reseller strategy, we've got some open questions around private deployments and commissioning.
00:12 Maya: great, quick intros — i'm Maya (AE), Jonah is our solutions engineer, Luca handles partner ops. maybe we do 10 minutes context, 20 technical, 10 for commercial and next steps? sound good?
00:22 Raj: yep that works. i'll kick off with context — PolarisIQ is building a verticalized search and summarization layer for legal docs, we run multi-tenant workloads across our customers and are exploring reseller/partner relationships to resell inference where we don't want to own GPUs.
00:36 Alex: our infra is AWS-heavy, VPCs across us-west-2 and eu-west-1, some on prem for regulated customers. latency SLOs are 50-100ms p95 for short queries, and larger batch summarizations up to 10k tokens where throughput matters.
00:49 Jonah: ok understood, quick clarifying Q: when you say reseller, do you mean PolarisIQ would rebrand Redwood-hosted endpoints, or do you intend to run Redwood Private inside your VPC and resell capacity?
00:58 Priya: both models are on the table, but first preference is reseller with Redwood hosted because onboarding is faster. however several of our enterprise customers require VPC or on-prem due to data residency, so that model needs to be possible too.
01:12 Maya: sensible. Redwood supports a hosted API, Dedicated reserved capacity for committed pools, and Private (VPC/on-prem) — we can do both. there are tradeoffs: hosted is fastest to launch and simplest for commissions, Dedicated gives predictable throughput, Private gives control but higher ops overhead.
01:28 Raj: on the ops overhead for Private, how heavy is the footprint? our infra team prefers small appliances not huge installs.
01:34 Jonah: good question — our Private package is designed to be lightweight — customer-managed control plane with a handful of nodes for small deployments. common confusions: the KV cache is a separate cache tier that we can either co-locate or run managed; sometimes people call it KV cash in notes, but it's KV cache.
01:49 Alex: haha yeah we've seen typos. For peak traffic we want autoscale but with strict p95 latency caps. does Redwood do smart routing across regions?
01:57 Maya: yes, smart routing can route by latency, cost, or customer tier. also automatic fallback to compatible model variants if capacity is constrained. worth flagging: for reseller commissions we can instrument usage per token and ship reports to you or to your customers depending on the arrangement.
02:12 Priya: on the subject of telemetry and security, SOC2 and audit logs are must-haves. do you support per-tenant audit trails and KMS integration?
02:20 Jonah: yes — per-tenant logs, KMS/HSM integrations supported. we'll share the security pack after the call. note our SOC2 doc is redacted for some vendor names but the controls are listed.
02:33 Priya: perfect. curious about quantization — we've seen model quality regress with aggressive quantization, but cost matters. what do you recommend?
02:41 Jonah: we have Optimize recommendations — model/quantization suggestions per workload. for short generation queries we lean to 4-bit quantized models with selective dequant for high-fidelity outputs; the platform can A/B roll quantization.
02:52 Raj: great. i want to deep dive later on KV cache coherence — when a user hits the same conversation across regions will the cache cause consistency issues?
03:02 Jonah: current approach is prefix/KV caching with awareness of region; we can replicate hot keys to reduce cross-region penalty, but strong consistency is not guaranteed out of the box — we can discuss strategies (sticky routing vs replicate) in the technical deep dive.
03:15 Alex: will need to run a real corpus against your runtime. can you support our tokenization and special markers?
03:21 Jonah: yes send a small sample, we can plug it into our bench harness. we typically run latency tests over three models: a low-cost open model, a mid-tier performant one, and an fp16 high-quality.
03:32 Priya: ok commercial questions: reseller margins and invoicing — will Redwood bill PolarisIQ or PolarisIQ bill end customers?
03:39 Maya: flexible — typical patterns: Redwood invoices PolarisIQ for usage (hosted) and PolarisIQ invoices end customers; for Dedicated and Private there are different licensing approaches. we have channel pricing tiers plus commission reporting. we'll send a partner terms sheet.
03:54 Raj: competitors question — our procurement asked about Anthropic and Vertex, how do you compare?
04:00 Maya: high level: we're positioning on production inference economics — predictable latency and tooling to keep costs low; not just model access. for some customers Anthropic or managed offerings may be ok but they lack our Dedicated/Private orchestration and observability.
04:14 Priya: good. one friction we foresee: onboarding enterprise customers that require SSO/SAML and long retention. can Redwood meet those?
04:22 Jonah: yes — SAML/SSO and RBAC are supported; retention windows are configurable. we'll share exact retention SLAs in the security pack.
04:32 Alex: about networking — for Private do you require open egress to the control plane or can it be fully air-gapped?
04:39 Jonah: Private has an option for air-gapped installs in our on-prem package but that adds support overhead and longer lead times; we can detail that in the next doc.
04:50 Priya: sounds reasonable. Luca, any partner ops questions from your side?
04:54 Luca: two things: reporting cadence (monthly usage exports) and lead attribution for co-sell — we need clarity so PolarisIQ can forecast.
05:02 Maya: we can do monthly exports and co-sell attribution via our partner dashboard; we'll include a sample CSV schema.
05:09 Raj: ok next steps recap?
05:12 Maya: recap: Redwood shares SOC2/security pack + partner terms (Maya by 3/7), Jonah runs a 2-hour benchmark with PolarisIQ sample corpus (by 3/11), PolarisIQ to provide traffic profile and topologies (Priya by 3/9), propose pilot kickoff week of 3/21 (Luca to send times).
05:28 Priya: confirmed. one ask — can you show Redwood Dedicated perf numbers for 1k qps with p95 80ms?
05:35 Jonah: we have internal perf decks, we'll surface an anonymized table in the benchmark doc.
05:42 Maya: great, thanks everyone — we'll follow up in email with links to security pack and a short summary.
05:48 Raj: thanks all, talk soon.

[End of recording]
